review_context: Enterprise Data Platform submitted UC as the foundational governance layer for the lakehouse. The TRB evaluated whether the metastore design and cross-region limitations meet the payer's multi-workspace governance model.
identified_risks: Metastore region lock-in limits disaster recovery
Admin burden for large permission matrices
mitigations: Delta Sharing used for cross-region workloads
Governance Hub provides centralized policy console
Role-based access templates for common personas
decision_rationale: UC is approved as the payer's single governance layer over all catalogs and PHI. The metastore region limitation is accepted as tolerable; cross-region PHI access will use Delta Sharing with explicit approvals.

review_context: Information Security presented UC audit logs as the immutable evidence source for HIPAA and SOC 2 audits. Retention, tamper-proof storage, and query performance were evaluated.
mitigations: Audit logs stored in managed UC tables with VACUUM restrictions
System tables provide efficient log queries
Tiered retention policy: hot 90 days, cold 7 years
decision_rationale: Audit logs are approved as the payer's audit source. Retention follows the enterprise records-retention policy (7 years), implemented by the platform team through audit-log delivery and system-table exports; all production workspaces must deliver audit logs.

review_context: Member Experience submitted the Salesforce connector (Lakeflow Connect) to sync Health Cloud and Service Cloud member and case data for a 360-degree member view. TRB is reviewing OAuth scope and PII field mapping to ensure minimum-necessary extraction.
identified_risks: Overly broad OAuth scope pulls unnecessary PII
Case comments may contain sensitive clinical notes
CRM deletion/archival timing vs. lakehouse retention
mitigations: OAuth scopes limited to standard Health Cloud objects
PII field mapping reviewed per data dictionary
Case comment fields excluded from initial sync
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Confirm final OAuth scope matches minimum-necessary and is documented. (2) Provide sample of member records synced to validate PII filtering. (3) Define CRM deletion sync behavior to align with 7-year retention. Follow-up at 2026-10-20.
open_questions: What is the final OAuth scope for member and case objects, and how does it match minimum-necessary?
Provide 10-row sample of member records to verify PII extraction boundaries.
How will Salesforce record deletions cascade to the lakehouse, and what retention period applies?
rereview_trigger: OAuth scope change or new use case

review_context: Claims Operations selected Auto Loader for continuous 837 EDI claim ingest and daily eligibility feeds. TRB evaluated file discovery mechanisms and guaranteed delivery semantics.
identified_risks: File notification latency for high-volume drops
mitigations: File notification mode used for high-volume feeds
Schema inference handles field additions automatically
Duplicate detection via file path and checksum
decision_rationale: Auto Loader is approved as the standard incremental ingestion path for claims and eligibility. File notification mode is required for high-volume EDI drops; directory listing is acceptable for lower-volume feeds.
rereview_trigger: Partner feed change or volume 10x increase

review_context: Claims Operations proposed DLT as the standard for building medallion (bronze/silver/gold) pipelines. TRB reviewed data-quality expectations, SCD handling, and audit capabilities.
identified_risks: Expectation failures hide data-quality issues if quarantine not monitored
SCD Type 2 complexity for member history
Pipeline dependencies not visible in lineage
mitigations: Expectations route bad rows to quarantine tables with alerts
APPLY CHANGES handles SCD Type 2 natively
DLT lineage integrates with UC governance hub
decision_rationale: DLT is approved as the enterprise standard for building and curating trusted claims and member tables. Expectation failures must be monitored; quarantine tables are part of the standard architecture.

review_context: Claims Operations and Finance jointly submitted Workflows (Lakeflow Jobs) as the enterprise orchestration engine. TRB evaluated task types, error handling, and audit logging.
identified_risks: Job dependencies not captured if manual coordination still used
Timeout handling for long-running claims joins
mitigations: Job DAG enforces explicit task dependencies
Timeout limits configured per task type
Each task execution logged to audit tables
decision_rationale: Workflows is approved as the enterprise standard for all scheduled and multi-step workloads. All production claims, eligibility, and reporting jobs must use Workflows.

use_cases: Time travel for audit and recovery
review_context: Enterprise Data Platform designated Delta as the default table format for all PHI workloads. TRB reviewed ACID guarantees, time-travel retention, and interoperability.
mitigations: VACUUM policy: 180-day retention for PHI, 30 days for analytics
Iceberg interoperability via UniForm
Delta version checks automated in CI/CD
decision_rationale: Delta Lake is approved as the default table format. All new tables use Delta unless approved for Iceberg. Time-travel and VACUUM retention are set per table to meet the records-retention policy.

review_context: Member Experience submitted Lakebase (managed Postgres OLTP) for powering member-facing apps with low-latency serving next to the lakehouse. TRB is reviewing backup/recovery, retention, and PHI-at-rest encryption.
identified_risks: Automatic backups may retain deleted PHI
Retention policy not aligned to HIPAA 6-year minimum
mitigations: Backup retention tuned to 7-year hold period
Automated backup lifecycle per retention policy
CMK applied to all Postgres instances
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Confirm backup retention policy covers 7 years for regulated data. (2) Verify CMK encryption covers Postgres storage at rest. (3) Provide recovery RTO/RPO guarantees. Follow-up at 2026-10-27.
open_questions: What is the backup retention policy for Lakebase instances handling PHI, and how is it enforced?
Does CMK encryption cover Postgres storage at rest, and how is key rotation managed?
What are the recovery RTO and RPO guarantees for Postgres backups?
rereview_trigger: Backup policy change or new retention requirement

review_context: Analytics Operations selected Databricks SQL (serverless warehouse) as the serving layer for analysts and BI tools querying PHI. TRB reviewed row/column filter enforcement and audit logging.
identified_risks: Filters bypassed if analysts query storage directly
Audit log volume for high-query-rate environments
mitigations: External table access restricted; SQL warehouse required
Warehouse queues configured per team SLA
Audit sampling for cost control; 100% for PHI modifications
decision_rationale: Databricks SQL is approved as the enterprise serving layer for BI and analytics. All BI tool connections must go through SQL warehouses. Row and column filters are enforced at query time.

review_context: Analytics Operations submitted AI/BI Dashboards for internal governance and reporting. TRB evaluated row/column filter enforcement in dashboards and viewer access controls.
mitigations: Filters re-evaluated on each refresh
Viewer access uses UC identities, no impersonation
Cache TTL set to 15 minutes for PHI dashboards
decision_rationale: AI/BI Dashboards are approved for internal governance and reporting with PHI filters. Dashboards must be built on UC tables with row/column masks enabled.

review_context: Analytics Operations submitted AI/BI Genie (natural-language Q&A) as an umbrella review for analyst self-serve access to PHI. Genie One (TRB-2026-005) is an existing approved use case. TRB is evaluating whether UC row/column masks and filters are proven to hold in Genie-generated SQL.
identified_risks: LLM prompt injection exposes schema or data
Genie answer cache leaks PHI between users
mitigations: Genie SQL generation goes through UC masking validation
User prompt validation and sanitization before LLM
Query result cache isolated per user with TTL
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Provide proof that UC row/column masks are applied in Genie-generated SQL for 5 test queries. (2) Demonstrate prompt injection mitigation. (3) Confirm cache isolation. Genie One has its own review (TRB-2026-005, Approved with Conditions); this umbrella review covers broader AI/BI Genie agent use with PHI. Follow-up at 2026-10-25.
open_questions: Provide test results showing UC row/column masks applied in Genie-generated SQL.
What prompt injection attacks have been tested and mitigated?
How is Genie query result cache isolated per user, and what is the TTL?
rereview_trigger: Genie architecture change or new foundation model

review_context: Research & Innovation selected MLflow as the system of record for ML model lifecycle (training, versioning, governance). TRB reviewed experiment tracking, parameter audit, and model promotion controls.
mitigations: MLflow experiments linked to UC tables via lineage
Model artifacts stored in UC volumes with versioning
Parameter comparison provided in MLflow UI
decision_rationale: MLflow is approved as the enterprise model registry and lifecycle system. All trained models must be logged to MLflow; promotion to production requires model-card sign-off.

use_cases: Real-time risk scoring on incoming claims
review_context: Research & Innovation submitted Model Serving for deploying trained models as low-latency APIs (e.g., real-time risk scoring on claims). TRB is reviewing network isolation and audit logging before scoring PHI.
identified_risks: API endpoint exposed to internet without auth
Model input/output not logged for audit
mitigations: Model endpoints run in private network with VPC endpoint
Request/response logging to audit tables with sampling
P99 latency target: <100ms for risk scoring
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Confirm endpoints run in private network accessible only via VPC endpoint. (2) Demonstrate audit logging for inference requests. (3) Validate latency meets claims-processing SLA. Follow-up at 2026-10-23.
open_questions: Are Model Serving endpoints restricted to private network access via VPC endpoint?
What inference request/response data is logged, and where is it stored?
What are the P50/P99 latency targets for risk-scoring APIs, and are they validated?
rereview_trigger: New model deployment or scoring use case

use_cases: Diagnosis code extraction from clinical notes
review_context: Analytics Operations submitted AI Functions (SQL) for calling foundation models directly from SQL to classify, extract, and summarize at scale. TRB is reviewing which foundation models are approved for PHI-bearing prompts.
identified_risks: LLM training data includes customer prompts and outputs
Uncontrolled model drift affects classification accuracy
Prompt injection reveals PII in classification result
mitigations: Foundation models vetted for no-training-data-retention guarantees
Model versioning controlled via Databricks Foundation Model API
Input sanitization and prompt injection validation
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Which foundation models have been approved by Legal/Privacy for PHI? (2) Provide no-training-data-retention guarantee from model provider(s). (3) Demonstrate input sanitization for classification prompts. Follow-up at 2026-10-24.
open_questions: Which foundation models (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) are approved for PHI-bearing prompts?
What is the no-training-data-retention guarantee from each approved provider?
What input sanitization is applied to prompts before sending to foundation models?
rereview_trigger: New foundation model or use case

review_context: Provider Strategy submitted Clean Rooms for joint analytics with provider networks where neither party exposes raw PHI. TRB is reviewing PHI handling in multi-party outputs and approval workflows.
identified_risks: De-identification logic insufficient for re-identification risk
Query results leak member-level PHI through aggregates
mitigations: De-identification rules reviewed by Chief Privacy Officer per-engagement
Output tables limited to summary statistics (counts, rates)
Collaborator dataset scan for PII before upload
decision_rationale: Under review. TRB asked: (1) Define de-identification thresholds and sign-off process. (2) Provide sample output tables and risk assessment. (3) Confirm Clean Room approval workflow includes CPO review. Follow-up at 2026-10-28.
open_questions: What de-identification thresholds and rules apply to Clean Room outputs?
Provide sample output tables and re-identification risk assessment.
What is the Clean Room approval workflow, and who must sign off?
rereview_trigger: New collaborator or use case change

review_context: Information Security presented Secure Cluster Connectivity (no-public-IP / NPIP) as a baseline network control for production PHI workloads. TRB reviewed routing and internet access constraints.
identified_risks: Public IPs still assigned if not configured correctly
Internet egress via NAT leaks IP source
mitigations: Cluster policies enforce no-public-IP setting
NAT gateway restricted to approved destinations
Egress firewall rules in network policies
decision_rationale: Secure Cluster Connectivity is approved and required for all production PHI workloads. All production clusters must have public IPs disabled.

review_context: Information Security proposed PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) for front-end and back-end connectivity, keeping all Databricks traffic off the public internet. TRB reviewed endpoint configuration and traffic isolation.
identified_risks: Front-end PrivateLink alone allows data egress via internet
Back-end PrivateLink adds cost and complexity
NAT gateway still needed for non-Databricks egress
mitigations: Dual PrivateLink (front + back) required for PHI workloads
Network policies restrict back-end routing
NAT gateway egress filtered to approved destinations
decision_rationale: PrivateLink is approved as a core requirement for the payer's PHI environment. Dual PrivateLink (front and back) is required for production PHI. Single PrivateLink is acceptable for non-PHI analytics.

use_cases: Encryption at rest with payer-controlled keys
review_context: Information Security selected Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for encrypting PHI at rest. TRB reviewed key lifecycle, HSM support, and key rotation automation.
identified_risks: Key loss disables all encrypted data
mitigations: Keys backed up in AWS KMS secure vault
Automated rotation via KMS key policy
KMS access controlled via IAM + UC external locations
decision_rationale: Customer-managed keys are approved and required for all PHI data at rest. Encryption must use CMK; AWS default keys are not acceptable for PHI.

use_cases: HIPAA posture for all PHI workloads
review_context: Information Security presented the Compliance Security Profile (CSP) as the master switch for HIPAA/PCI/FedRAMP posture. TRB reviewed hardened images, audit requirements, and permanent enablement.
identified_risks: Permanent CSP flag blocks certain features
Image updates may have performance impact
mitigations: CSP feature matrix documented (limits known upfront)
Performance impact quantified (<5% CPU overhead)
Audit sampling tuned to balance cost vs. visibility
decision_rationale: The Compliance Security Profile is approved and required for all PHI workloads. Once enabled on a workspace, it cannot be disabled. All production PHI workspaces must have CSP enabled.

review_context: Compliance Officer submitted the HIPAA profile as the specific security and privacy posture for the payer's regulated data. TRB reviewed controls mapping to 45 CFR 164 Privacy and Security Rules.
identified_risks: Controls incomplete for all HIPAA subparts
Breach notification workflow not in Databricks
mitigations: Controls matrix maps UC features to 45 CFR 164 controls
Breach procedures documented in payer playbook (out-of-band)
SSO/SCIM enforces identity provider training compliance
decision_rationale: The HIPAA profile is approved as the payer's standard security and privacy posture for PHI. All PHI workspaces must enable the compliance security profile with the HIPAA compliance standard selected, under the signed BAA.

review_context: Information Security selected Enhanced Security Monitoring (ESM) to add malware, file-integrity, and vulnerability monitoring on compute handling PHI. TRB reviewed agent overhead and alert handling.
mitigations: Agent overhead <5% CPU; tuned sampling rates
Alert thresholds and allowlists reduce false positives
Serverless compute ESM roadmap exists but not yet approved
decision_rationale: Enhanced Security Monitoring is approved for production PHI workloads on classic compute. ESM is required for all production clusters running PHI. ESM coverage for serverless compute is to be confirmed with the account team.

review_context: Information Security proposed SSO and SCIM (via Okta) for centralized identity management and automatic deprovisioning. TRB reviewed IdP failover and access revocation timing.
mitigations: IdP redundancy via multiple Okta instances
SCIM sync runs every 15 minutes; max 15-min lag
Cluster policies forbid local user creation
decision_rationale: SSO and SCIM are approved and required for enterprise access control. All users must authenticate via Okta SSO. Local accounts are prohibited for PHI workspaces.

use_cases: This feature tracker weekly refresh job
review_context: Enterprise Data Platform submitted Databricks CLI for automation and this tracker's weekly refresh workflow. TRB reviewed credential handling and audit logging.
identified_risks: CLI audit trail sparse vs. web console
mitigations: API tokens limited to service principals with short TTL
CLI calls logged via audit tables
GitHub Actions tokens use temporary credentials
decision_rationale: The Databricks CLI is approved for platform-team tooling and automation. CLI is restricted to service-principal identities. Human API tokens are discouraged.

review_context: Enterprise Data Platform selected Asset Bundles (DABs) as the enterprise deployment standard for jobs, pipelines, and apps. TRB reviewed version control integration and rollback procedures.
identified_risks: DAB validation doesn't catch breaking changes
mitigations: DAB syntax validation in pre-commit hooks
Automated rollback via Git revert
Deployment windows scheduled weekly
decision_rationale: Asset Bundles are approved as the enterprise deployment standard. All production jobs and pipelines must be deployed via DABs. Manual resource creation is prohibited.

use_cases: Elastic batch processing for claims jobs
review_context: Finance selected Serverless Compute to reduce idle costs for bursty claims and reporting jobs. TRB is approving with conditions on compliance security profile validation and cost attribution.
identified_risks: Compliance security profile not available on serverless
mitigations: Compliance security profile roadmap confirms PHI support Q4 2026
Spend controls via serverless job capacity reservations
Isolated pools for high-priority workloads
decision_rationale: Serverless Compute is approved with conditions. PHI workloads require the compliance security profile enabled before production use. Condition COND-034-1 requires CSP GA on serverless; COND-034-2 requires cost attribution implementation; COND-034-3 requires performance baseline. Follow-up at 2026-08-16.

conditions.title: Compliance Security Profile (CSP) GA on Serverless
conditions.text: Databricks must release CSP support for serverless compute. PHI workloads are blocked until CSP is GA and validated on serverless.
conditions.rationale: PHI workloads require CSP hardening; CSP is not yet available on serverless.
conditions.verification_method: Databricks product release notes and feature availability documentation

conditions.title: Cost Attribution to Claims Operations
conditions.text: Implement cost allocation for serverless jobs so Claims Operations can track DBU spend. Tagging must enable per-job and per-team cost reporting.
conditions.rationale: Finance needs visibility into serverless costs to optimize and attribute to business units.
conditions.verification_method: Cost analysis report showing serverless job costs tagged by team and workload

conditions.title: Performance Baseline for Claims Jobs
conditions.text: Run 5 pilot claims jobs on serverless (100-500GB datasets) and document P50/P99 latency vs. classic compute. Startup overhead must be <5 min.
conditions.rationale: Claims processing SLAs require validated latency to ensure serverless meets production requirements.
conditions.verification_method: Performance benchmark report with job latency distributions and startup times

rereview_trigger: CSP on serverless GA or Compute strategy change

review_context: Enterprise Data Platform maintains Classic Compute as a strategic compute option for workloads requiring specific instance types or network controls not available via serverless.
mitigations: Cluster auto-termination policies enforced
Cluster policies lock critical settings
Gradual migration to serverless as gaps close
decision_rationale: Classic Compute is approved for production workloads where serverless is not suitable. Cluster policies are required; all production clusters must use an approved Databricks Runtime LTS version, with Photon where supported.
